To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The sequences controlling the DNA damage-mediated induction of the R. capsulata recA and uvaA genes were identified.

(a) the recA and uva genes of R. caps. are regulated at the transcriptional level by the SOS system, and that (b) the consensus sequence controlling the SOS induction of the Rhodopirilaceae family is the GTTCVY VYTWTGTTC motif.

the recA and uxrA SOS promoters of the Rhodopseudobacteriaceae family share the consensus sequence GTTCTTCTTCTTTTGTTC, and that this sequence is also present upstream of the uxaA and uxaB genes, which encode enzymes of the pentose phosphate pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the Rhodopirillaceae SOS operator sequence and its functional characterization.
the identification of the DNA sequences controlling the expression and the induction of the recA and uvirA genes of R. caps. and R. spher.
the characterization of the SOS system of R. caps.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SOS operator site is composed of a core element (GTTC) and a variable element (VYVYT).
the Rhodospiraillaceae SOS operators are composed of a core sequence, GTTC, which is flanked by two variable regions of 3 and 4 nucleotides, respectively.
the GTTCVYVTWTGTTC consensus sequence is the operator for the Rhodobacteria family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite their phylogenetic divergence, the Rhodospillaceae family has a common mechanism to control expression of the SOS DNA repair genes.
the SOS system of the Rhodopseudomonaes is not only regulated by the LexA repressor, but also by the RpoH sigma factor, which is a member of the ECF family of sigma factors.

the SOS operators of Rhodospirilaceae are not identical to the consensus SOS operators of the Enterobacteriaceae and Bacillus families, which are characterized by the GTTCN8GTTC and GTTAN8TTC consensus sequences, respectively.
